topic.angle: Why +50% then -50% is not back to even

card.title: Up 50%, down 50%, not back to even

body.claim: A 50% rise followed by a 50% fall leaves you below where you started.
body.why: Each percentage is measured against a different starting amount. A 100 that rises 50% becomes 150, but 50% of 150 is 75, so the fall lands on 75. In general, an increase of x percent followed by a decrease of x percent ends with a net decrease.

probes.question: A $200 price rises 10%, then falls 10%. What is the final price?
True or false: a 25% increase is undone by a 25% decrease.

claims.claim: A 100 that rises 50% becomes 150, and 50% of 150 is 75 (title, claim, why)
claims.note: Verified by calculation: 100 x 1.5 = 150; 150 x 0.5 = 75, below 100.

claims.claim: An increase of x percent followed by a decrease of x percent ends with a net decrease
claims.quote: hence the net change is an overall decrease by x percent of x percent

claims.claim: Each percentage is measured against a different starting amount (percent changes do not cancel)
claims.quote: a percentage increase requires a different percentage decrease to return to the original value

claims.note: Verified by calculation: 200 x 1.1 = 220; 220 x 0.9 = 198. Also stated on the page ($198, not the original $200).

claims.claim: Probe: a 25% increase is not undone by a 25% decrease
claims.quote: a 25% increase ($100 to $125) must be followed by a 20% decrease ($125 to $100) to restore the initial amount
